title: High CO2 on the ventilator in a wheezy young man
summary: A 24-year-old man with a severe asthma attack has a high CO2 but stable blood pressure on a low ventilator rate.
rationale: Moderate expiratory obstruction with a safe rate (RR 12) gives modest auto-PEEP and tolerable hypercapnia; increasing RR to 26 stacks breaths. Headless engine check on the starting settings and after the named actions: untouched by 2 min: PaCO2 64, pH 7.22, SpO2 98%, Pplat 10, auto-PEEP 2.9, SBP 122; untouched by 60 min: PaCO2 67, pH 7.20, SpO2 98%, Pplat 10, auto-PEEP 2.9, SBP 122; reasonable management by 60 min: PaCO2 67, pH 7.20, SpO2 98%, Pplat 8, auto-PEEP 0.7, SBP 124; typical mistake by 60 min: PaCO2 32, pH 7.44, SpO2 99%, Pplat 18, auto-PEEP 10.7, SBP 100. Values for an arm whose case ended early (improved or deteriorated trigger) are the values when it ended.

retestsMistake.clinicalFocus: Accept permissive hypercapnia (pH above about 7.15-7.20) in asthma; raising the rate to normalise PaCO2 causes auto-PEEP and hypotension

source: The Ventilator Book 3e (obstructive disease / auto-PEEP chapters, numbers unverified); Marino ICU Book 2025 (severe asthma and COPD exacerbation chapters, numbers unverified); Nunn & Lumb 9e (airway resistance chapter, unverified); Darioli R, Perret C. Mechanical controlled hypoventilation in status asthmaticus. Am Rev Respir Dis 1984;129:385-7; Marino ICU Book 2025 (ventilator management in asthma, unverified). Expiratory resistance 55 is a teaching assumption (unverified).

changes.vignette: Male 24, 178 cm (PBW 73 kg), 72 kg. VC 480 mL, RR 12, flow 70 L/min, PEEP 0.

patient.presentingStory: Intubated 2 hours ago for a severe attack. The ABG shows PaCO2 63 and pH 7.22. The blood pressure is stable. A colleague suggests raising the rate to "get the CO2 normal".
patient.history: Atopic asthma, poor adherence to inhalers. Full escalation.

actions.text: You disconnect the ventilator. A short rush of air escapes from the endotracheal tube over a few seconds. The blood pressure is unchanged.

orderEffects.note: Apnoea trial / ventilator disconnection permits complete exhalation of trapped air
Inhaled beta-2 agonist and anticholinergic reduce bronchospasm
Systemic corticosteroid anti-inflammatory action occurs over hours
Intravascular volume expansion partially counteracts intrathoracic pressure on venous return

then.text: Nurse notes: Expiratory hold shows auto-PEEP is high! The systolic pressure is dipping on the monitor.

then.detail: Maintaining or increasing set respiratory rate (>= 20 bpm) in severe bronchospasm leads to dynamic hyperinflation, severe auto-PEEP, and hemodynamic collapse.
Applying high external PEEP (>= 10 cmH2O) in passively ventilated asthma adds directly to alveolar pressure and exacerbates hyperinflation and hypotension.

then.text: His blood pressure is stable, the peak pressures have dropped and the dynamic hyperinflation is resolving.

then.reason: Obstructive strategy applied successfully: dynamic hyperinflation resolved, auto-PEEP lowered, and hemodynamic collapse averted.

then.text: The patient is in severe obstructive shock with unrecordable blood pressure and pulseless electrical activity!

then.reason: Severe dynamic hyperinflation and auto-PEEP caused complete loss of venous return and PEA arrest.
